donor_source_ids: Blackwell, D. (1951), Comparison of Experiments, Proc. Second Berkeley Symposium
Blackwell, D. (1953), Equivalent Comparisons of Experiments, Ann. Math. Statist. 24(2)
verification aids: Richet-Perez proof note (HAL hal-03393159); de Oliveira diagrammatic notes; Liang lecture notes ch4 (five equivalent definitions); Tamuz Caltech notes
donor_structure: Experiment = Markov kernel mu(.|theta) from state theta to signals. mu' is a GARBLING of mu iff mu' = mu.M for a stochastic (Markov) matrix M. Theorem: garbling iff statistical sufficiency iff mu is preferred by EVERY expected-utility decision maker in every decision problem (one partial order, several equivalent definitions).
target_structure: HSG representation sufficiency atom: when does a representation r: Sigma -> R of the search state preserve everything the system needs? Representation r2 is sufficient relative to r1 iff r1 factors through r2 by a degradation kernel; equivalently r1 loses no task value over r2 iff r2 is a garbling of r1.
mapping: experiment mu(.|theta) <-> observation channel induced by representation r; garbling matrix M <-> any coarser representation r' = M.r (deterministic or stochastic aggregation); decision problem u <-> HSG task; value order <-> uniform-over-tasks value of a representation.
preserved_relations: garbling order is a partial order (reflexive, transitive); so representation sufficiency is transitive: composing degradations loses (weakly) value
strictly coarsening a representation strictly loses value for SOME task (not all) - coarsening is never free but is sometimes harmless
sufficiency = existence of a factorization through a kernel: purely structural, prior-free
d = 0 distance under bisimulation metrics (Desharnais 2004) recovers the exact/aggregation end of the same order (kernel-side dual)
known_broken_relations: Blackwell order is partial: incomparable representations exist (no total preorder on representations); HSG must keep incomparability, not force a ranking
classic theorem is finite signal/state spaces; general Borel extensions exist but measurability conditions must be added (assumption iii relocation, same caveat as G01/G06 rows)
unknown_correspondences: Blackwell order with COSTLY observation (channel price) - the price-aware refinement relevant to G10 burden is not part of the parent theorem
whether the PAC-Bayes chain geometry (G17 receipt) is monotone along the Blackwell order of its data-dependent priors - open, candidate D13 question
assumptions_added: fixed task family (decision problems) known to the comparison - 'every task' quantification is over a declared family
representations as measurable kernels (no nonmeasurable representations; ties to assumption iii load-bearing finding in G06 row)
candidate_theorem: HSG representations ordered by garbling: r1 >= r2 iff exists kernel M with r2 = M.r1; then r2 suffices for every governed task iff r1 does, and if the order is strict some task loses value. Corollary: representation-minimal systems sit at garbling-minimal elements of their reachable representation set; further compression is exactly the Blackwell-incomparable-or-worse region.
strongest_parent: Blackwell 1951/1953 garbling-sufficiency-value equivalence (verified at L2 and re-checked at validate)
route: proof route: direct - the parent theorem IS the transported statement modulo renaming; finite case immediate, Borel case by standard extension
self_assessment_note: parent verified against multiple independent sources; mapping is a renaming, so SUPPORTED rather than PROPOSAL; residual risk concentrated in the Borel-extension measurability caveat
